# n8n-manager-mcp - MCP Server for n8n Workflow Management

> n8n-manager-mcp is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI assistants like Claude, Cursor, and Windsurf manage n8n workflows end-to-end: list, create, update, delete, activate, export, import, and inspect executions. Connects directly to the n8n REST API with no Python dependency, and supports multiple n8n instances at once.

19 tools cover workflow listing, reading, creation, updating, deletion, activation, execution inspection, export/import, safety settings, backups, node descriptions, server profiles, server reachability, and optional manager history. `n8n_describe_nodes` returns short descriptions of common node types, not complete schemas. Multi-server support routes to configured n8n instances. When `backup_before_mutations` is enabled (default: true), snapshots are attempted before update, delete, activate/deactivate, and overwrite-restore operations; a failed enabled backup stops the following n8n mutation request. Create/import have no pre-mutation backup; import creates a new workflow without a rollback handle. Local audit logging is configurable and enabled by default. `N8N_MANAGER_READ_ONLY=1` adds an environment-level ceiling to the persisted read-only setting. The server loads configuration before checking the mutation gate, and a blocked mutation may append to the local audit log.

Verification (2026-11-02): fresh `npm test`, build, smoke discovery, and
package dry-run pass with 208 Vitest tests (100% pass).
The 2026-11-02 audit of the unreleased source lockfile reports zero known advisories.
It locks @hono/node-server 2.1.6 and qs 6.17.1, above the patched floors for
GHSA-rmxm-3fg6-px4f and GHSA-6pq8-jhm2-2vcw; every other locked package version is preserved.
The package dry-run contains the built server and smoke discovery reports all
19 tools.

Part of the ellmos family. Node.js, MIT. Published as `n8n-manager-mcp` on npm. Publicly listed on Glama, Enterprise DNA, and PulseMCP under the ellmos-ai namespace. Some MCP ecosystem indexes still expose the legacy `io.github.lukisch/n8n-manager-mcp` entry; this repository includes `server.json` for the ellmos-ai namespace.

## Audience

- AI assistant users who work with n8n and want to manage workflows via Claude, Cursor, or Windsurf
- Developers building AI agents that automate workflow orchestration via n8n
- DevOps and automation engineers integrating n8n into AI-assisted pipelines
- Power users managing multiple n8n instances and needing AI-driven workflow operations
- Open-source contributors exploring MCP server development with TypeScript and Node.js

Backup path segments are sanitized and resolved under the configured backup root. Real-path and symlink checks apply to backup, listing, and restore operations; listing returns regular JSON backup files. These checks are scoped to those operations and do not establish general immunity to all filesystem escapes or malformed inputs. `servers.json`, backup files, and the audit log are local plaintext; newly written config files request POSIX mode `0600`, while Windows access follows directory ACLs. Audit append errors propagate and may occur after a remote mutation has succeeded. Network requests go to configured n8n endpoints and, when enabled, the manager endpoint; the update notifier may check for updates on interactive TTY startup and skips this check in non-TTY stdio operation. The reviewed application source contains no product-analytics sender.

`n8n_add_server` preserves an existing default when `is_default` is omitted on update; `true` promotes and explicit `false` removes the flag, with first-server fallback when no default remains.
